Is there anything I can do for you?
I hardly ever go outside,
so I don't know much about the world...
Oh, welcome,

en: I've been expecting you.
note: Follows the name + '.' (#143)

en: Having you visit me,

en: it somehow takes my mind off things.

en: I'm doing some sewing right now.
I hardly ever go outside, you see...
Forgive me, but who might you be?
I am Veta.
For Grandfather's sake,
I'd like to make him a feather pillow,
or so I keep thinking, but
note: Cut at the same point as the Japanese; continues in #2336 after the button

en: I just can't seem to gather enough down...
I'm so worried about Grandfather.
A doctor is attending him, but
the doctor seems distracted by other things.
note: Subject (the doctor) restored; no pronoun because the doctor's gender is unknown

en: I'm good at sewing, but
that alone is no help to Grandfather,
and that makes me sad.
I'm worried about Grandfather's illness...
When you come to see me,
The doctor is attending him, but
that alone is no help to Grandfather, and
note: Variant wording of #2341/#2342 split differently; 'and' carried here so #2347 reads 'that makes me sad.'

en: that makes me sad.
You are a kind person.
That kindness of yours,
note: Continues in #2350 (separate message, no end marker)

en: I'd like a share of it, too.
Just during the night is enough.
And only until this battle is over.
Quickly... give me your orders.
note: Follows '{PLAYER_NAME}, my master...' (#0); Emmy is entranced

en: Please... please, give me your orders...
Good... morning.
note: Hesitant, broken greeting kept

en: Is something the matter...?
note: Preceded by 'Um...' (#2218)

en: It's gotten quite cold already, hasn't it?
I'm in a hurry, I'm afraid...
I really must hurry and
finish my winter preparations...
note: Msg 115989 uses #2418 + '...': #2418 needs 'finish my winter preparations' without the dots

en: It's gotten chilly, hasn't it?
It has really turned cold lately,
so please take care.
Excuse me, what is it?
note: Works for both continuations (#2365 and #2421-#2423)

en: I'm resting. Please go away.
What on earth do you want?
Oh, it's you.
If you're idle enough to visit me,
I'd like you to help me make hay.
note: Subject 'I' restored

en: Coming to see me again,
you must have a lot of free time.
I was just about to have tea.
Would you like to join me?
You could stay and relax a while, you know.
note: Subject 'you' restored

en: Um, is there something you need?
The weather's nice today, you see,
and this is when you get good hay,
so I'm very busy.
You... is there something you need?
I'm very busy, you know.
Anyway, it has to be put out in the sun
note: Referent 'it' = the hay (inferred from context); sentence continues in #2382

en: as much as possible.
If you were the sun,
I'd want you to stay here the whole time, you know.
(Everything that woman says grates on me...)
note: Inner thought of the protagonist about Emmy

en: Without this,
cows and horses have nothing to eat in winter.
If the cows and horses suffer, people will soon suffer too.
That's how it is.
(And if the humans are gone,
we are in trouble too... is that it...?)
note: Inner thought; 'we' = vampires, kept as in the source

en: Phew
This much should be just about enough.
Oh, you

en: You stayed right to the end, didn't you?
Did this really interest you that much?
note: Shared by msgs 115759 and 116300; works in both

en: Yes, I find it interesting.
(Humans with strength or skill
have good blood, after all.)
